inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments - equity settled transactions' GBP 11.7m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp); EquityAwardTaxes nil in every year (awards settled from employee share trusts funded by the ~GBP 10m/yr own-share purchases)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average 259.5m at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim note 7: 258.0m basic + 1.5m dilutive employee share awards). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the ~GBP 10m/yr own-share purchases by the employee trusts are what keep the count flat in practice (basic count 258.0m vs 258.7m in FY2022).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence sterling (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote pence. Fixed ratio, no FX risk and no parity check needed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the flows' currency: UK 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free, 5.0% ERP, beta 1.1 for a mining-equipment cyclical with ~80% aftermarket revenue gives cost of equity ~10%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.1% (net finance cost guided ~GBP 90m on ~GBP 1.8bn gross debt, 26% tax); debt ~17% of EV at the current price. WACC = 0.83 x 10.0 + 0.17 x 4.1 = 9.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios -- cyclicality, leverage and integration risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Net debt GBP 1,448.6m at 30 June 2026 is the company's own definition and INCLUDES GBP 154.4m IFRS 16 lease liabilities; lease principal (~GBP 35m/yr) is NOT deducted from the flows. Adjusted EBITDA is post-IFRS-16, D&A (3.5% of revenue) includes right-of-use depreciation (~GBP 30m), and capex_pct of 3.7% = 2.5% cash capex (FY2025 PPE 60.0 + intangibles 5.2 = 65.2 on 2,564.5) + ~1.2% right-of-use asset renewal, so the ongoing lease cost is charged once through the capex-like line. Lease interest is inside net finance cost, i.e. below the unlevered flows and captured by the net-debt deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (GBP 0.7m of FY2025 profit, ~GBP 10m of equity, <4p/share) and are not deducted; flows are modelled on a consolidated basis. The ESEL Chile JV buyout completed Q1 2026 removed the main remaining minority.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, scenario-weighted -- Weir is an operating industrial (mining equipment and ~80% aftermarket parts), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the owner-fcf-adaptations (GBP WACC, single lease treatment, SBC-light market). First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF. OWNER FCF ANCHOR: FY2025 reported FCF 320.2 (OCF 385.4 after GBP 132.0m tax paid, before interest, less capex 65.2) minus SBC 11.7 = 308.5. interest_income is 0 because Weir is a net-debt company (GBP 1.45bn) and interest received (GBP 9.8m FY2025) sits in investing activities, outside reported FCF. FY0 BUILD CHECK: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA 608.2 (23.7% margin), adjusted operating profit ~518 (20.2%), implied D&A inside adjusted EBITDA ~90 (3.5%); the component build on FY2025 inputs gives ~370 of FCF vs 308.5 actual, the gap being the GBP 34m working-capital outflow and ~GBP 30m of exceptional/restructuring cash (Performance Excellence, total programme cost GBP 113m finishing in 2026) that adjusted EBITDA excludes. The driver paths therefore carry an 'owner EBITDA margin' ~0.5-0.7pp below adjusted EBITDA margin in FY2026 and ~0.3pp thereafter, since Weir books adjusting items every year. TIMING: FY0 is FY2025; year 1 is FY2026, of which H1 is reported (revenue +6.2%, adjusted op margin 18.8%, net debt/EBITDA 2.2x). The June 2026 net debt already embeds H1 FY2026 cash flow (owner FCF ~GBP 54m, ~21p/share, <1% of value) so there is a small double count in the price-neutral direction; accepted and noted. CASH TAX: FY2025 cash tax 132.0 on ~518 of adjusted EBIT = 25.5%; UK statutory 25%, group adjusted ETR guided mid-20s; 26% flat on EBIT, no ramp needed. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer -- receivables + inventory exceed payables (FY2025 WC outflow GBP 34m, H1 FY2026 conversion 41% on inventory build), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE at -20% of the revenue change. TERMINAL: cap set at 16x owner FCF; Gordon at 9%/2.5% is 15.8x so Gordon binds in base -- a cyclical cap in the 12-15x band would cut value a further ~2%. The current price implies ~27x trailing owner FCF (EV ~GBP 8.3bn / 308), i.e. the market already pays a terminal multiple the house model does not grant.
inputs.price_note: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2254-3580p

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025), corroborated by management's mid-single-digit organic FY2026 guidance and mid-to-high single digit through-cycle target; equity 5yr CAGR 7.8% is inflated by the FY2020 trough base (post O&G impairments)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.8% vs revenue 3yr CAGR 1.2%: >30% divergence. Revenue 3yr is depressed by FX translation (GBP 22m PBT headwind in FY2025 alone) and the FY2022 post-divestment rebound base; equity 5yr starts from the FY2020 impairment trough. Neither is a clean trend; 5.5% selected as the through-cycle organic rate.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2020 185.2 -> FY2022 250.1 -> FY2025 308.5. Owner-FCF CAGRs are ~0.3pp below reported because SBC grew from 9.3 to 11.7, but SBC is <0.5% of revenue so the gap is immaterial. EPS 5yr CAGR is undefined (FY2020 EPS -0.576 on O&G exit losses). FY2016-FY2021 history includes the Oil & Gas division divested in 2021; only FY2022 onward is pure continuing mining.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +7.0% reported: H1 +6.2% reported, FY guidance of mid-single-digit organic growth plus the stub-year contribution of Micromine (consolidated from 30 Apr 2025), Townley (Aug 2025), Fast2Mine (Nov 2025) and ESEL (Q1 2026). FY2027-30 decelerate 6.0 -> 4.5%, the low end of the mid-to-high single digit through-cycle target, since the valuation is being struck near a copper/gold price high; glide to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_note: Owner EBITDA margin: FY2025 adjusted 23.7% less ~0.5pp exceptional cash. FY2026 23.5% reflects the guided ~50bps adjusted operating margin expansion (to ~20.7%) less the final ~GBP 25m of Performance Excellence cash; H1 was 18.8% so the full year depends on the usual H2 weighting. Matures at 24.5% (adjusted ~24.8%, op margin ~21.3%) -- management targets 'sustainably above 20%' op margin; software mix supports modest further expansion.

scenario_narratives.base: Mining capex stays supportive on structural copper/critical-minerals demand and brownfield debottlenecking, and the ~80% aftermarket base compounds with the installed fleet. FY2026 lands on guidance (mid-single-digit organic growth, ~50bps adjusted margin expansion, 90-100% cash conversion after the weak 41% H1) and net debt/EBITDA returns toward 1.5x by year end. Growth decelerates from 7% to the low end of the mid-to-high single digit through-cycle target, since we are valuing near a commodity-price high. Owner EBITDA margin matures at 24.5% (adjusted op margin ~21%) as Performance Excellence savings land and Micromine/Fast2Mine software mix grows, but no credit is given for the >22% that the bull case needs. New CEO Andrew Neilson executes the existing strategy without a reset.
scenario_narratives.bull: The critical-minerals supercycle thesis plays out: copper supply deficits drive a sustained OE project wave into FY2029, aftermarket intensity rises with declining ore grades, and Weir's share gains (Vertical Stirred Mills, WARMAN MCR2, Nexsys GET; >90% mill-circuit trial win rate) hold pricing against Chinese replicators. Micromine ARR compounds >25% and the equipment-agnostic software layer lifts group margin to 26% owner EBITDA (adjusted op margin ~23%) while the Townley/ESEL foundries take out cost. Faster deleveraging funds further bolt-ons. Terminal growth 3% and an 18x cap reflect a higher-quality, more software-weighted mix.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns in FY2027: a global slowdown or a copper price reversal cuts OE orders hard (revenue -6% then -2%, in line with Minerals' 2015-16 experience; the 80% aftermarket cushions but does not immunise -- miners defer rebuilds and switch to replicator parts when cash is tight), owner EBITDA margin troughs at 19.5% on under-absorbed foundries and an integration hangover from four simultaneous acquisitions. Deleveraging stalls with net debt/EBITDA above 2x into the downturn and the ~GBP 90m interest bill bites. Recovery from FY2029 at 3-4% but margin only rebuilds to 22% as the new CEO consolidates rather than expands. Terminal growth 2% and a 14x cyclical cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25%: the valuation is struck near a copper/gold price high, net debt/EBITDA is 2.2x (above the 0.5-1.5x range) with GBP 1.8bn of gross debt, four acquisitions are being integrated at once, H1 FY2026 showed margin slippage and 41% cash conversion, and the CEO changed on 1 August 2026 -- several of the bear axes are already visible. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (a sustained OE wave, software-driven margin to 26% and durable aftermarket pricing against replicators). Base 50%: guidance has been reiterated three times this year and the aftermarket model has historically delivered.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Weir is a high-quality, aftermarket-dominated mining-equipment franchise with real switching costs, but it is priced for the supercycle: the current price is ~27x trailing owner FCF and ~16x adjusted EBITDA, at a cycle high and with leverage elevated by the Micromine deal. The house model gives full credit for guided FY2026 delivery and a 24.5% mature owner EBITDA margin but refuses to capitalise a terminal multiple above what Gordon at a 9% GBP WACC allows. On that basis the weighted intrinsic value sits below the price; the gap is the price of the re-rating already embedded in the share. SBC is <0.5% of revenue so the house/street band is a few pence wide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mining capex / commodity cycle: copper, gold and iron ore drive both OE orders and, with a lag, aftermarket intensity; the bear case alone is worth roughly a third of the base value
Leverage: net debt/EBITDA 2.2x at June 2026 and ~GBP 90m/yr of net interest; a downturn before deleveraging completes squeezes equity
Integration of Micromine, Townley, Fast2Mine and ESEL under a new CEO; H1 FY2026 margin (-100bps) and cash conversion (41%) already show strain
Replicator / low-cost competition on aftermarket parts, the core of the margin structure
FX translation: a largely USD/AUD/CLP business reporting in GBP (GBP 22m PBT headwind in FY2025); the GBP WACC and terminal growth assume no persistent sterling strength
Terminal value is roughly 55-60% of EV in the base case; each 0.5pp of WACC is worth ~8-10% of value
